The dubious evidence for sunshine supplements



Tim Cross

Senior science writer



 Most doctors are dubious about the merits of supplements, pointing out that many of them have no evidence to suggest that they are safe, or that they work as advertised. If that sounds like fussiness, it is actually the voice of bitter experience. Medicine is full of treatments that looked good on paper, but turned out to be useless—or even harmful—in the real world.
